name: Hyderabad–Raipur Expressway
history: The road between Hyderabad and Raipur runs through some of the least developed and most heavily forested country in central India, across the Godavari valley and the districts of eastern Maharashtra and southern Chhattisgarh. The existing route is slow and winding. This planned expressway takes a much more direct line, and it is intended as much to open up that interior as to shorten the drive between the two state capitals.
facts: Would link the capitals of Telangana and Chhattisgarh directly for the first time.
Crosses the forested districts of eastern Maharashtra and southern Chhattisgarh.
Aims to cut a journey of more than eleven hours to around seven.
It would connect the Hyderabad industrial region to the Chhattisgarh steel and coal belt.
Part of the Bharatmala programme of new national corridors.
significance: Central India's mineral belt and the industry around Hyderabad trade heavily with each other, but the roads between them still wind through hill and forest. A direct corridor would also give some of the country's remotest districts their first fast road.
